common_name: Prairie Dusk Penstemon (Cold-Hardy Rose-Purple Hybrid Beardtongue)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; Prairie Dusk is a Nebraska-bred hybrid penstemon noted for excellent cold hardiness and reliable perennial return, though in the Gulf South it especially needs sharp drainage to avoid winter and summer root rot in humid, poorly drained soil.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun, choosing a raised or sloped site if garden soil tends to stay wet; Prairie Dusk is a hybrid penstemon developed in Nebraska from a cross of Penstemon barbatus and Penstemon strictus, bearing tall spikes of tubular, rose-purple flowers in early summer that are a strong draw for hummingbirds and bumblebees. It is notably cold-hardy and, given the sharp drainage penstemon generally demands, an easygoing, long-lived perennial in climates with well-drained soil. In humid Gulf Coast gardens, good drainage matters more than fertility for success — amend heavy clay with grit or plant on a raised berm to keep the crown from sitting in wet soil, which is the most common cause of penstemon failure in the region. Deadhead spent spikes to tidy the plant and encourage a possible light rebloom.
